title: Garments and Categories
summary: Students move from studio tools to the garments they design, sketch, and describe. They learn core garment names, sort garments into simple fashion categories, understand short spoken and written descriptions, and produce a scaffolded Garment ID Card using A2 sentence frames.
essential_question: How can I identify, group, and describe common garments in simple English for Fashion Design study?
professional_context: Week 3 connects English to the visible objects of Fashion Design work: tops, bottoms, one-piece garments, outerwear, and simple looks. Students need this language to talk about what they draw, sew, present, organize, and later critique in class and portfolio contexts.
grammar_focus: plural forms such as pants, jeans, and shorts
teacher_preparation: Preview the Week 3 garment boards, the three-description reading board, and the listening script before class.
Prepare visible sentence frames for This is a ___, These are ___, It has ___, They have ___, and It is for ___.
Review the Week 3 correction targets, especially missing articles and singular-plural agreement with pants, jeans, and shorts.
Decide whether students will build the Garment ID Card from a projected image set, printed cards, or a future app gallery.
Bring or project garment image cards for the teacher-led pronunciation, category sorting, and speaking session.
student_deliverables: Completion of the garment opener and recognition task.
Completion of the core garment vocabulary matching set.
Reading-comprehension responses about three garment descriptions.
Listening-comprehension responses identifying garments from short spoken descriptions.
Completion of garment phrase practice using singular and plural sentence frames.
A scaffolded Garment ID Card with 5 to 6 required sentence-frame lines and one optional challenge line.
One corrected Week 3 sentence saved after review.
A short teacher-observed oral garment presentation.
